description: 《This Is Me》描寫一個人長期受到歧視、嘲笑與排斥後，逐漸學會接納自己、勇敢展現真實面貌的成長過程。歌中的主角曾因自己的缺點與傷痕感到羞愧，甚至相信自己不值得被愛。然而，她終於決定擺脫外界的批評與偏見，不再隱藏內心的脆弱，而是勇敢站出來，為自己的存在感到驕傲。歌曲以尖銳的言語、子彈與洪水等意象，象徵傷害、反抗與突破束縛的力量。最終，《This Is Me》傳達的是自我接納、勇氣與尊嚴：每個人都有獨特的價值，即使曾經受傷或被否定，也值得獲得愛與尊重。只要願意相信自己，便能勇敢面對世界，活出真正屬於自己的人生。

vocabulary.meaning: 對某種經驗或情況很熟悉，通常因為已經經歷多次。
vocabulary.usage: `be no stranger to + 名詞／V-ing`，常接壓力、辛苦、挑戰等經驗。
options: The new bridge is no stranger to the river because it is made of steel.
I no stranger to long trips, so I always bring a map.
Our science teacher is no stranger to strange questions; we ask her about aliens every Friday.
The museum no stranger to at nine o'clock each morning.
optionExplanations: 鋼製橋樑不是因為材質就「熟悉」河流；此片語描述有經驗的主體。
少了 be 動詞，應說 I am no stranger to long trips。
老師經常遇到奇怪問題，因此對這種經驗「不陌生」，語意與句型都正確。
少了 be 動詞，而且營業時間不能這樣接在片語後；可說 The museum opens at nine。
vocabulary.explanation: 老師經常遇到奇怪問題，因此對這種經驗「不陌生」，語意與句型都正確。

vocabulary.word: Be ashamed of — 對……感到羞愧
vocabulary.meaning: 因為某件事感到不好意思、羞恥或後悔。
vocabulary.usage: `be ashamed of + 名詞／V-ing`；也可以用 `be ashamed to + 動詞`。
options: My brother was ashamed of tell the coach that he lost the ball.
I felt ashamed of my mistake, so I went back and told the truth.
The train was ashamed of arriving at six because it had four doors.
She was ashamed of to sing in front of the class.
optionExplanations: 介系詞 of 後面不能直接接原形動詞；應說 ashamed of telling 或 ashamed to tell。
因自己的錯誤感到羞愧並誠實承認，搭配與意思都正確。
火車有四扇門與「羞愧」沒有合理關係；可說 The train arrived at six。
ashamed of to sing 結構錯誤；應說 ashamed to sing 或 ashamed of singing。
vocabulary.explanation: 因自己的錯誤感到羞愧並誠實承認，搭配與意思都正確。

vocabulary.word: As you are — 以你原本的樣子
vocabulary.meaning: 不必改變自己目前的樣子或狀態。
vocabulary.usage: 常出現在 `accept/love someone as they are`；也可說 `Come as you are`（照你現在的樣子來）。
options: The director said, “Come as you are; this party has no dress code.”
I will repair the computer as you are because its screen is broken.
We drove as you are from Rome to Paris in one day.
The pianist played the song as you are on a very old piano.
optionExplanations: 派對沒有服裝規定，因此可以穿著原本的樣子來，符合固定說法。
修理電腦應說 as it is 或直接說 repair the broken computer，不能用 you 指電腦。
as you are 不表示交通方式或行程；可說 We drove from Rome to Paris。
這裡要描述演奏方式，不能用指人的 as you are；可說 He played the song beautifully。
vocabulary.explanation: 派對沒有服裝規定，因此可以穿著原本的樣子來，符合固定說法。

vocabulary.word: Break someone down — 使某人精神崩潰、失去信心
vocabulary.meaning: 困難、批評或壓力逐漸削弱一個人的信心或精神。
vocabulary.usage: `break + 人 + down`；注意 `break down` 也可指機器故障，但意義不同。
options: Three years of unfair criticism almost broke her down, but her team helped her recover.
The mechanic broke the car down by washing its windows.
The astronaut broke down her helmet because she wanted to see the stars better.
The football player broke down the score by kicking the ball into the goal.
optionExplanations: 長期不公平的批評幾乎摧毀她的信心，符合「精神被擊垮」的用法。
洗車窗不會表示讓車子故障；可說 The mechanic cleaned the windows。
這句想說摘下頭盔，應用 took off her helmet，不是 broke down。
踢球得分應說 scored a goal；break down 不表示得分。
vocabulary.explanation: 長期不公平的批評幾乎摧毀她的信心，符合「精神被擊垮」的用法。

vocabulary.word: Drown out — 用更大的聲音蓋過
vocabulary.meaning: 一個聲音太大，讓另一個聲音聽不見。
vocabulary.usage: `drown out + 聲音／人說話的聲音`，例如 `The music drowned out my voice`。
options: The map drowned out the hikers because they were looking for a path.
The concert drums drowned out the guide's voice, so nobody heard the tour rules.
My phone drowned out its battery when the screen went black.
The chef drowned out the soup by adding a little pepper.
optionExplanations: 地圖不能用「聲音蓋過」登山客；可說 The map confused the hikers。
鼓聲蓋過導覽員的說話聲，正是 drown out 的典型用法。
手機沒電應說 ran out of battery，不是 drowned out its battery。
加胡椒是在調味，不是用聲音蓋過；可說 The chef added pepper to the soup。
vocabulary.explanation: 鼓聲蓋過導覽員的說話聲，正是 drown out 的典型用法。

vocabulary.meaning: 身體因撞擊而出現瘀青；也可形容自尊或感情受傷。
vocabulary.usage: `a bruised knee`、`feel bruised after criticism`；不要和 `broken` 混淆。
options: After the basketball game, Leo had a bruised arm but no broken bones.
The history book was bruised because it had twenty chapters.
Our flight was bruised by two hours because of the weather.
She bruised the mountain by taking a photo of it.
optionExplanations: 打球碰撞造成手臂瘀青，bruised arm 是正確搭配。
書有很多章節不會因此「瘀青」；可說 The book has twenty chapters。
航班延誤應用 delayed，不是 bruised。
拍照不會讓山瘀青；可說 She photographed the mountain。
vocabulary.explanation: 打球碰撞造成手臂瘀青，bruised arm 是正確搭配。

vocabulary.word: Be meant to be — 注定如此；本應如此
vocabulary.meaning: 某事彷彿命中注定，也可以表示事情原本就應該那樣。
vocabulary.usage: `It was meant to be`（這似乎是命中注定）；`be meant to + 動詞` 則可表示預定用途或應做之事。
options: The museum tickets were meant to be inside the printer because they were blue.
Mia and Zoe met on the same train three times; they joked that their friendship was meant to be.
The driver meant to be the bus at six without any other verb.
My new password was meant to be because it has eight letters.
optionExplanations: 票券顏色與命中注定無關；若指應放的位置，可說 The tickets were supposed to be in the printer。
兩人巧遇多次，開玩笑說友誼是命中注定的，符合片語意思。
meant to be the bus 意思不通；若要說司機本來應六點到，應說 The driver was meant to arrive at six。
密碼有八個字元不足以說明「命中注定」；可說 My password has eight letters。
vocabulary.explanation: 兩人巧遇多次，開玩笑說友誼是命中注定的，符合片語意思。

vocabulary.word: March on — 堅定地繼續前進
vocabulary.meaning: 像行軍一樣往前走；也可比喻在困難後繼續努力。
options: We marched on the email by clicking “Reply.”
The scientist marched on the water until it became ice.
The actor marched on his lines by forgetting every word.
The dancers marched on despite the rain and finished the street parade.
optionExplanations: 回覆電子郵件應說 replied to the email，不是 marched on。
讓水結冰應說 froze the water，不是 marched on the water。
忘記台詞不是「堅持前進」的搭配；可說 The actor forgot his lines。
表演者即使下雨仍堅定前進，marched on despite the rain 很自然。
vocabulary.explanation: 表演者即使下雨仍堅定前進，marched on despite the rain 很自然。

vocabulary.word: Sink in — （消息或感受）逐漸被理解、接受
vocabulary.meaning: 某件事需要一點時間，人才真正意識到它或感受到它。
vocabulary.usage: `The news finally sank in`；不要和字面上的 `sink into water`（沉入水中）混用。
options: The new bus timetable sank in the station because it was printed in green.
Our football coach sank in the team when the match ended.
When the email arrived, I read it twice before the news finally sank in: I had won the art contest!
I sink in a sandwich every morning before school.
optionExplanations: 綠色的時刻表不會因此被「理解入心」；可說 The timetable was posted at the station。
sink in 通常是不及物片語，不能這樣直接接球隊當受詞；可說 The coach spoke to the team。
得獎消息過了一會兒才真正讓人意識到，the news sank in 非常自然。
吃三明治應用 eat；sink in 不等於「吃進去」。
vocabulary.explanation: 得獎消息過了一會兒才真正讓人意識到，the news sank in 非常自然。

vocabulary.meaning: 因為行為、努力或本身的價值而值得某種待遇或結果。
vocabulary.usage: `deserve + 名詞`；`deserve to + 動詞`，例如 `You deserve a break`。
options: The spaceship deserves to the moon every Tuesday.
I deserve of a trophy because I won the chess match.
The library deserves at seven because the doors are open.
After helping the whole class prepare for the show, our teacher deserves a day off.
optionExplanations: deserve to 後面必須接原形動詞；若指飛往月球，可說 The spaceship travels to the moon。
deserve 是及物動詞，不需要 of；應說 I deserve a trophy。
開門時間應用 opens at seven，不是 deserves at seven。
老師辛苦協助準備表演，值得放假一天，deserves a day off 用法正確。
vocabulary.explanation: 老師辛苦協助準備表演，值得放假一天，deserves a day off 用法正確。

questions.meaning: 躲起來；把自己藏起來
questions.usage: 不想被看見或想避開別人時；可說 hide away from people。
options: The singer hid away her song on the stage.
They hid away to the bus stop at six.
He hid away in his room to avoid the crowd.
She hid away the door before going home.
optionExplanations: 錯：此處想表達在台上演唱，不是躲藏。
錯：hide away 不表示前往車站。
對：躲在房間裡避開人群，符合躲藏的意思。
錯：關門應用 closed the door。
questions.explanation: 對：躲在房間裡避開人群，符合躲藏的意思。

questions.meaning: 疤痕；（比喻）過去傷痛留下的痕跡
questions.usage: 可談皮膚上癒合後的傷疤，或難忘的情感傷害。
options: The doctor scarred the news to my family.
He wore his scars to keep the rain off.
Her scars were new cuts that had not healed yet.
The old scars on his arm came from a fall.
optionExplanations: 錯：scar 不能代替 told 或 explained。
錯：scars 不是可穿戴的雨具。
錯：尚未癒合的新傷口通常叫 cuts 或 wounds，而非 scars。
對：舊傷留下的疤痕，scars 用法正確。
questions.explanation: 對：舊傷留下的疤痕，scars 用法正確。

questions.meaning: 光輝燦爛的；令人讚嘆的
questions.usage: 形容美麗壯觀的景象、成功時刻，或令人感到榮耀的事情。
options: I glorious the dishes after dinner.
She has three glorious in her bag.
We saw a glorious sunset over the sea.
This train glorious at seven each day.
optionExplanations: 錯：glorious 是形容詞，不是洗碗的動詞。
錯：glorious 不是可數名詞。
對：壯麗的夕陽可以用 glorious 描述。
錯：句中缺少動詞，不能拿 glorious 當動詞。
questions.explanation: 對：壯麗的夕陽可以用 glorious 描述。

questions.meaning: 最尖銳的；最鋒利的（sharp 的最高級）
questions.usage: 描述刀刃最鋒利，或言語特別刻薄、傷人。
options: Her sharpest words made her friend cry.
This was the sharpest rain of the day.
He sharpest the knife every week.
The cake is sharpest because it is sweet.
optionExplanations: 對：尖銳傷人的言語可用 sharpest words。
錯：一般不以 sharpest rain 形容雨量或強度。
錯：sharpest 不是磨刀的動詞；應用 sharpens。
錯：甜味不是 sharpest 在這裡的意思。
questions.explanation: 對：尖銳傷人的言語可用 sharpest words。

questions.meaning: 洪水；大量湧來的事物
questions.usage: 形容水大量淹沒地區，也可引申為訊息或情緒大量湧入。
options: She bought a flood to wear in winter.
The flood covered the road after heavy rain.
We flooded to school by bus every day.
The flood was small enough to fit in my cup.
optionExplanations: 錯：flood 不是可穿的衣物。
對：豪雨後淹過馬路，是 flood 的字面用法。
錯：flood 不是搭公車去上學。
錯：洪水不是能裝入杯中的小量水。
questions.explanation: 對：豪雨後淹過馬路，是 flood 的字面用法。

questions.meaning: 不為自己的選擇道歉；坦然堅持立場
questions.usage: 強調自己不因正當立場而感到抱歉；不代表犯錯時也拒絕道歉。
questions.prompt: 哪一句正確使用「make no apologies」？
options: I make no apologies with a knife and fork.
I make no apologies for speaking up against unfair rules.
We make no apologies the window each morning.
She made no apologies to go by bus each day.
optionExplanations: 錯：這個片語不能表達使用餐具。
對：對反對不公平規定的立場不感到抱歉，語意清楚。
錯：片語不能代替開窗動作。
錯：搭公車不是 make no apologies to go 的用法。
questions.explanation: 對：對反對不公平規定的立場不感到抱歉，語意清楚。

questions.meaning: 子彈（bullet 的複數）
questions.usage: 描述武器發射的彈丸；歌詞以子彈比喻傷人的批評。
options: The teacher wrote bullets from her pen onto paper.
He opened the window with two bullets of air.
The police found two bullets near the broken wall.
Her new shoes were full of music bullets.
optionExplanations: 錯：若指條列項目，要說 bullet points，不是筆寫出的子彈。
錯：空氣不能用 bullets 計數。
對：在牆附近發現子彈，使用正確。
錯：music bullets 不是一般自然搭配。
questions.explanation: 對：在牆附近發現子彈，使用正確。

questions.meaning: 儘管問；儘管說（口語）；字面也可指開火
questions.usage: 當別人想問很多問題時，可以說 Fire away! 表示歡迎提問。
options: If you have more questions, fire away!
Her lunch fired away because it was cold.
I fire away to school at eight every day.
Please fire away the book onto my desk.
optionExplanations: 對：表示歡迎對方繼續提問，是常見口語說法。
錯：午餐變冷不是 fire away 的意思。
錯：fire away 不表示走去學校。
錯：放書到桌上應用 put the book on my desk。
questions.explanation: 對：表示歡迎對方繼續提問，是常見口語說法。

questions.meaning: 猛然衝破；突然穿過
questions.usage: 形容人或物以強大力量穿過障礙，也可用於突破限制的比喻。
options: My sister was bursting through her breakfast slowly.
I was bursting through the blue of the sky.
The letter burst through to my phone at noon.
The runners were bursting through the finish line tape.
optionExplanations: 錯：吃早餐不自然地使用 burst through。
錯：the blue of the sky 不是明確可衝破的障礙。
錯：接收訊息不用 burst through to my phone。
對：跑者衝破終點線綵帶，表示突然有力地穿過。
questions.explanation: 對：跑者衝破終點線綵帶，表示突然有力地穿過。

questions.meaning: 路障；阻擋通行的障礙物
questions.usage: 描述道路、入口為阻止通行而設的阻擋設施；也可比喻限制。
options: Workers put barricades across the road for safety.
We drank barricades with dinner at home.
She wore barricades when the rain began.
The barricades told us what time it was.
optionExplanations: 對：施工安全需要在道路設路障，搭配正確。
錯：路障不是飲料。
錯：路障不是雨衣。
錯：路障本身不會報時。
questions.explanation: 對：施工安全需要在道路設路障，搭配正確。

questions.meaning: 戰士；勇敢努力的人（比喻）
questions.usage: 可以指戰鬥的人，也可形容面對困難、努力奮鬥的人。
options: Our warriors tasted sweet with the rice.
She warrior the homework after school.
The bus is warriors because it is early.
The story is about warriors who protected their town.
optionExplanations: 錯：戰士不是食物。
錯：warrior 是名詞，不能代替做功課的動詞。
錯：warriors 不是形容公車準時的形容詞。
對：故事中保護城鎮的戰士，語意正確。
questions.explanation: 對：故事中保護城鎮的戰士，語意正確。

questions.meaning: 值得……；配得上……
questions.usage: 用 be worthy of + 名詞或 V-ing，表示值得尊重、信任或獎賞。
options: Her hard work is worthy of our respect.
This old chair is worthy of to sell tomorrow.
He worthy of finished his work at six.
They are worthy of very quickly to school.
optionExplanations: 對：她的努力值得尊重，worthy of + 名詞。
錯：介系詞 of 後不能直接接 to sell。
錯：缺 be 動詞，且不能接 finished 作此句型。
錯：of 後面不能這樣接副詞及方向片語。
questions.explanation: 對：她的努力值得尊重，worthy of + 名詞。

questions.meaning: 伸手去拿；努力爭取
questions.usage: 可表示手伸向物品；比喻努力追求願望時也常見。
options: I reached for my dinner by eating very fast.
She was reaching for the book on the top shelf.
The boy reached for to his pencil on the table.
We reached for to the park on the bus.
optionExplanations: 錯：吃得快不等於伸手拿取或追求。
對：伸手去拿高架上的書，使用自然。
錯：reach for 後面直接接名詞，不加 to。
錯：reach for 不能代替搭車去公園。
questions.explanation: 對：伸手去拿高架上的書，使用自然。

structure.title: 句型研習
structure.note: 依提供的核對版材料編排；保留原有教學範圍。

questions.word: be no stranger to + 名詞
questions.meaning: 對某種經驗不陌生，可能已經經歷多次。
questions.usage: 談工作挑戰、旅途或反覆遇到的情況。
questions.prompt: 情境： 一位導遊經常遇到下雨天。 選出最符合本節句型且文法、語意自然的一句。
options: The guide is no stranger to rainy days.
The guide no stranger to rainy days.
The guide is no stranger for rainy days.
The guide is no stranger to rainly.
optionExplanations: 正確：be no stranger to 後接名詞 rainy days。
錯：缺少 be 動詞 is。
錯：固定介系詞是 to，不是 for。
錯：rainly 不是可在這裡使用的名詞。
questions.cue: I'm not a stranger to the dark（PDF 原歌詞第 2–3 頁）
questions.explanation: 正確：be no stranger to 後接名詞 rainy days。

questions.meaning: 省略主詞 you，直接提出命令或請求。
questions.usage: 給人即時指示；歌中是他人要求歌者躲藏，並非歌者認同的話。
questions.prompt: 情境： 捉迷藏開始前，哥哥叫大家躲起來。 選出最符合本節句型且文法、語意自然的一句。
options: You hide away behind the tree now, please?
To hide away behind the tree now.
Everyone hides away before I count.
Hide away behind the tree before the game starts.
optionExplanations: 錯：這是以 you 開頭的敘述式語序，不是目標祈使句。
錯：to hide 是不定詞片語，不能單獨作完整祈使句。
錯：這是直述句，不是本題要的直接祈使句。

questions.usage: 談一個消息或想法慢慢被理解。
questions.prompt: 情境： 收到錄取通知後，一位演員過了好久才相信。 選出最符合本節句型且文法、語意自然的一句。
options: The news took a minute to sinking in.
The news took a minute to sink into.
The news took a minute to sink in.
The news took a minute to sink in it.
optionExplanations: 錯：to 後接原形 sink。
錯：sink into 後需要受詞，而非句末單獨使用。
正確：sink in 可指消息慢慢被理解。
錯：sink in 在此不需 it 作受詞。
questions.cue: I won't let the shame sink in（PDF 原歌詞第 2–3 頁）
questions.explanation: 正確：sink in 可指消息慢慢被理解。

questions.meaning: 描述當下正在發生的動作。
questions.usage: 描述大家眼前正在進行的活動。
questions.prompt: 情境： 小隊正在為戲劇演出布置舞台。 選出最符合本節句型且文法、語意自然的一句。
options: The team building the stage right now.
The team is built the stage right now.
The team is building the stage right now.
The team are build the stage right now.
optionExplanations: 錯：building 前缺少 is。
錯：is built 是被動或其他形式，不是正在建造。
正確：is building 表正在布置。
錯：are 後需 building，不能直接用 build。
questions.cue: We are bursting through the barricades（PDF 原歌詞第 2–3 頁）
questions.explanation: 正確：is building 表正在布置。

questions.meaning: 用力衝破障礙；歌詞把路障作社會限制的比喻。
questions.usage: 描述水流、陽光等穿過阻礙的畫面。
questions.prompt: 情境： 暴風雨後陽光穿過雲層。 選出最符合本節句型且文法、語意自然的一句。
options: The sun burst the clouds through to.
The sun burst to through the clouds.
The sun burst through from the clouds.
The sun burst through the clouds.
optionExplanations: 錯：名詞受詞應接在 through 後。
錯：burst through 不再加 to。
錯：through 後直接接 clouds，不必加 from。
正確：burst through the clouds 表強力穿過雲層。
questions.cue: bursting through the barricades（PDF 原歌詞第 2–3 頁）
questions.explanation: 正確：burst through the clouds 表強力穿過雲層。

questions.meaning: 伸手去拿或努力觸及某個目標。
questions.usage: 描述伸手去拿高處物品，或比喻努力爭取。
questions.prompt: 情境： 小孩伸手要拿架上的故事書。 選出最符合本節句型且文法、語意自然的一句。
options: The child reached to for the book on the shelf.
The child reached for to the book on the shelf.
The child reached for the book on the shelf.
The child reached the for book on the shelf.
optionExplanations: 錯：reached to for 重複介系詞。
錯：for 後不再加 to。
正確：reached for + 名詞 book。
錯：the for book 語序錯誤。
questions.cue: reaching for the sun（PDF 原歌詞第 2–3 頁）
questions.explanation: 正確：reached for + 名詞 book。

questions.word: 現在完成式：have/has + 過去分詞
questions.meaning: 強調直到現在發生的改變所造成的結果。
questions.usage: 回顧從過去到現在的成長。
questions.prompt: 情境： 兩位朋友多年練習後成為好廚師。 選出最符合本節句型且文法、語意自然的一句。
options: We are become good cooks after years of practice.
We have become good cooks after years of practice.
We have became good cooks after years of practice.
We has become good cooks after years of practice.
optionExplanations: 錯：are become 不是此處的現在完成式。
正確：have + 過去分詞 become。
錯：become 的過去分詞是 become，非 became。
錯：we 應配 have，不配 has。
questions.cue: that's what we've become（PDF 原歌詞第 2–3 頁）
questions.explanation: 正確：have + 過去分詞 become。

questions.meaning: 表示值得某事；歌詞有否定用法，重點仍是值得尊重和愛。
questions.usage: 談表現是否值得肯定、努力是否值得稱讚。
questions.prompt: 情境： 義工幫忙了一整天，值得感謝。 選出最符合本節句型且文法、語意自然的一句。
options: The helpers are worthy for our thanks.
The helpers worthy of our thanks.
The helpers are worthy of our thanks.
The helpers are worthy to our thanks.
optionExplanations: 錯：此搭配使用 of，不是 for。
錯：worthy 前缺少 are。
正確：be worthy of our thanks。
錯：worthy of + 名詞，不是 worthy to + 名詞。
questions.cue: I'm not worthy of（PDF 原歌詞第 2–3 頁）
questions.explanation: 正確：be worthy of our thanks。

questions.word: nothing + 省略受詞關係子句／雙重否定
questions.meaning: nothing 與 not 的組合強調「沒有任何不值得的事」；of 的受詞就是前面的 nothing。
questions.usage: 讀懂帶否定的複雜句，不誤解為「我什麼都不值得」。
questions.prompt: 情境： 導遊表示這裡沒有她不熟悉的街道。 選出最符合本節句型且文法、語意自然的一句。
options: There is anything I do not know about.
There is nothing I do not know about it.
There is nothing I am not knowing about.
There is nothing I do not know about.
optionExplanations: 錯：anything 在肯定存在句中不能取代 nothing 表相同意思。
錯：about 的受詞已在前面，不需再加 it。
錯：know 通常不用 am knowing 表這種一般知識。
正確：nothing + I do not know about，about 的受詞為 nothing。
questions.cue: There's nothing I'm not worthy of（PDF 原歌詞第 2–3 頁）
questions.explanation: 正確：nothing + I do not know about，about 的受詞為 nothing。

questions.meaning: 表示每一次某種情況發生時。
questions.usage: 描述反覆出現的事件及相應反應。
questions.prompt: 情境： 每當下雨時，公園的青蛙就會叫。 選出最符合本節句型且文法、語意自然的一句。
options: Whenever does it rain, the frogs sing in the park.
Whenever raining, the frogs sing in the park.
Whenever it rains, the frogs sing in the park.
Whenever it rain, the frogs sing in the park.
optionExplanations: 錯：時間子句不用問句倒裝 does it rain。
錯：這裡缺少主詞 it。
正確：Whenever + it rains，完整子句。
錯：it 第三人稱單數應用 rains。
questions.cue: Whenever the words wanna cut me down（PDF 原歌詞第 2–3 頁）
questions.explanation: 正確：Whenever + it rains，完整子句。

questions.meaning: 用不定詞表目的，意思是「為了……」。
questions.usage: 解釋某項行動的目的。
questions.prompt: 情境： 工作人員關門以免音樂吵到附近居民。 選出最符合本節句型且文法、語意自然的一句。
options: They closed the door to keep the noise down.
They closed the door to keeping the noise down.
They closed the door for keep the noise down.
They closed the door keep the noise down.
optionExplanations: 正確：to keep 引出關門的目的。
錯：目的不定詞 to 後接 keep，不是 keeping。
錯：for 後不能接原形 keep 表目的。
錯：缺少目的不定詞的 to。
questions.cue: to drown them out（PDF 原歌詞第 2–3 頁）
questions.explanation: 正確：to keep 引出關門的目的。
